articleBody:
Hanging drywall in a basement requires preparing the foundation, framing, and indoor environment long before lifting the first sheet. Use this practical preparation checklist to ensure a long-lasting finish.

- [ ] Measure basement relative humidity with a hygrometer — Humidity should consistently sit below 60%, ideally between 30% and 50%, to protect building materials.
- [ ] Inspect concrete foundation walls for seepage — Moisture sources must be fully repaired and dried before installing framing or wallboard.
- [ ] Verify pressure-treated lumber is used for bottom plates — Wood resting directly against concrete slabs must resist ground moisture transfer.
- [ ] Frame around plumbing valves, cleanouts, and meters — Code requires permanent access openings for critical home utility shutoffs.
- [ ] Check stud spacing and wall alignment with a long level — Straight, plumb studs prevent wavy drywall seams and cracked joint compound later.
- [ ] Confirm rough-in electrical and plumbing work is complete — Running wires or pipes after drywall is fastened causes expensive wall demolition.
- [ ] Select appropriate drywall panels for below-grade spaces — Standard drywall installed against damp environments can deteriorate and require total replacement.
- [ ] Clean floor slab perimeter and clear work areas — Dust and construction debris interfere with bottom plate fastening and floor-to-wall clearances.

How to use this checklist:
Walk your basement with this list prior to ordering drywall sheets. Resolving foundation and moisture items early keeps your remodel on schedule and prevents costly wall teardowns.
